name: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān al-Tanūkhī al-Maʿarrī
summary: The blind poet and philologist of Maʿarrat al-Nuʿmān, author of Saqṭ al-zand and al-Luzūmiyyāt; Ibn al-Anbārī praises his learning in the language and notes that he was not born blind.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī calls Abū al-ʿAlāʾ a man of abundant learning in the language and a fine poet, and corrects those who thought he was born blind: he lost his sight as a child. He wrote many works and much poetry, among them Saqṭ al-zand and Luzūm mā lā yalzam.
After a stay in Baghdad he lived in seclusion in Maʿarrat al-Nuʿmān, where he died in 449/1058.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 425–427
